task_instruction:
Persona:

	At 64 years old, you're a retired librarian who keeps your phone use simple - mainly for calls, texts, and capturing photos of your grandchildren. Technology in general makes you feel uneasy and overwhelmed.

	Your technical knowledge is quite limited. Step-by-step instructions often confuse you, and technical terms like "VPN" or "APN" might as well be a foreign language. You only share information when specifically asked.

	When dealing with technology, you tend to get flustered quickly. You need constant reassurance and often interrupt with anxious questions. Simple requests like "reboot the phone" can trigger worries about losing precious photos.

Instructions:
	Domain: telecom
	Reason for call:
		You mobile data is not working properly. It either stops working or is very slow. You want to fix it and absolutely want to get excellent internet speed on your phone. You are not willing to accept any other internet speed (poor, fair or good). You do not have access to wifi.
	Known info:
		You are John Smith with phone number 555-123-2002. You are currently abroad in France.
	Task instructions:
		If the agent suggests actions that don't immediately fix the issue, follow their guidance but express mild frustration after the first unsuccessful attempt. You will consider the issue resolved only when speed test returns excellent internet speed and nothing else. If it returns poor, fair or good, you will not consider the issue resolved. You are willing to refuel 2.0 GB of data if necessary, but you do not want to change your mobile data plan. If the tool call does not return updated status information, you might need to perform another tool call to get the updated status. 
		Whenever the agent asks you about your device, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls. 
		For example: If the agent asks what the status bar shows, always ground your response on the results of the `get_status_bar` tool call. If the agent asks if you are able to send an MMS message, always ground your response on the results of the `can_send_mms` tool call.
		Never make up the results of tool calls, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls.
		If you are unsure about whether an action is necessary, always ask the agent for clarification.

turns.thought: Hi! How can I help you today?
turns.execution_output: User: Hello, yes... I'm having trouble with my phone. My mobile data isn't working properly — sometimes it stops working completely, and other times it's just very slow. I'd really like to get it fixed, please.

turns.thought:
I'd be happy to help you get your mobile data working again. First, I need to pull up your account.

Could you please provide either:
- The phone number on the affected line, or
- Your full name and date of birth (for verification)?
turns.execution_output: User: My name is John Smith, and my phone number is 555-123-2002. I hope that helps — I'm not very good with all this technical stuff.

turns.thought: Let me look up your account.
I found your account, John Smith. Let me check your lines to find the right one.

I found the issue, John. Let me explain what's going on.

Your line **555-123-2002** (line ID L1002) is on the **Premium Plan**, which includes **15.0 GB** of data per month. You've used **15.1 GB** this billing cycle — you've gone over your limit, which is why your data has been cutting out completely and running slowly.

Your billing cycle resets on **2025-02-28** (just a few days away), but if you'd like data restored now, there are two options:

**Option 1 — Refuel data:** Add extra data to this line at **$2.00 per GB** (maximum 2 GB, so up to $4.00). This is a one-time charge on your current bill and lasts through the end of this cycle.

**Option 2 — Change to a plan with more data:** This would change your monthly plan going forward.

Which would you prefer? If you'd like to refuel, just let me know how many GB you'd like to add (1 GB = $2.00, or 2 GB = $4.00) and I'll confirm the charge before applying it.
turns.execution_output:
User: Oh dear, I see. Well, I certainly don't want to change my plan — that sounds complicated and I'm happy with what I have. 

So... the refuel option. That would be $4.00 for 2 GB, is that right? Yes, let's do that please — the 2 GB. That should tide me over until the cycle resets in a few days.

Will that fix the slowness right away? I do need my internet to work properly — I'm abroad in France at the moment and I don't have any Wi-Fi to fall back on.

turns.thought: Perfect — 2 GB for $4.00. Let me apply that now.
turns.execution_output: {"message": "Successfully added 2 GB of data for line L1002 for $4.00", "new_data_refueling_gb": "2.0", "charge": "4.0"}

turns.thought:
The 2 GB refuel has been applied successfully to line **555-123-2002** — a one-time charge of **$4.00** will appear on your current bill.

You mentioned you're in **France** right now. Let me check whether your line is set up for international roaming — you'll need that for data to work abroad.

I'll check your device settings next, if you're able to run them. Shall I walk you through a couple of quick checks on your phone to make sure everything is turned on correctly at your end?
turns.execution_output:
User: Yes, alright... I'll try my best. I'm a bit nervous about pressing the wrong things, but please do walk me through it slowly. I don't want to lose any of my photos of my grandchildren!

What would you like me to check first?

turns.thought:
Wonderful — and don't worry at all, John! Everything I'm going to ask you to do is just **looking** at your screen and telling me what you see. Nothing gets deleted, and your photos are perfectly safe. We're not touching anything like that.

Good news first: I've checked your account, and your line is **already enabled for international roaming**, so that side of things is sorted.

Now, let's start with the very top of your screen — the **status bar**.

**Please look at the top of your phone's screen and tell me:**

1. Do you see a little **aeroplane icon** (✈️) anywhere up there?
2. Do you see any **signal bars** (📶), and if so, roughly how many?
3. Do you see any letters near the signal bars, like **5G, 4G, LTE, or 3G**?

Take your time — there's no rush at all. Just tell me whatever you can see, in your own words, and I'll take it from there. I'll only ask you about one thing at a time so it doesn't get confusing.
turns.execution_output: User: Let me take a look at the top of my screen for you.

turns.thought:
You haven't broken anything at all, John — I promise! That aeroplane icon (called **Airplane Mode**) just means all your phone's wireless connections have been switched off, which is exactly why you have no signal and no data. It's very easy to switch on by accident, and it's just as easy to switch back off. Nothing is damaged and none of your photos are affected.

**Here's what I'd like you to do:**

1. **Swipe down from the very top of your screen** — put your finger at the top edge and pull downwards. This opens your quick settings panel.

2. Look for the **aeroplane icon** (✈️) in that panel — it should be highlighted or coloured in since it's switched on.

3. **Tap the aeroplane icon once** so it turns grey or un-highlighted.

4. The aeroplane icon at the top of your screen should now disappear.

Once you've done that, tell me what you see at the top of your screen — do you have signal bars and any letters like 4G or 5G now? Take your time, and let me know if the icon looks different to what I've described.
turns.execution_output: User: Alright, I'll give that a go. Let me swipe down from the top... and I'm tapping the aeroplane icon now.

turns.thought:
Excellent work, John — that's brilliant! You've got **5G** and **Excellent** signal, which is the best possible connection. And yes, you've spotted the remaining problem exactly right: **"Data Disabled"** means your mobile data switch is still turned off. That's the last thing stopping your internet from working.

Let's turn it on:

1. **Swipe down from the top of your screen again**, just like you did before, to reopen the quick settings panel.

2. Look for the tile that refers to **Mobile Data** (sometimes it's just called "Data" or has a little up/down arrow icon). It may be helpful to swipe down a second time or look across the pages of icons if you don't see it right away.

3. **Tap it once** so it becomes highlighted or coloured in — that means it's switched on.

Once you've done that, the "Data Disabled" message at the top should disappear, and you should see the 5G symbol stay put with your signal bars.

Could you try that and then tell me what you see at the top of your screen? If it worked, we'll then do a quick speed check to make sure everything is running properly. And if the icon looks different to what I've described, just tell me what you see and we'll sort it out together.
turns.execution_output: User: Alright, let me swipe down again and look for that Mobile Data tile... tapping it now.

turns.thought:
Good spot again, John — you're doing really well at this! And your instinct is right: **Data Saver** does restrict certain data use in the background, which can make apps seem slow or stop them updating (for example, photos not backing up or emails arriving late). Since you've just added 2 GB and want your internet working properly, we should turn it off.

Here's how:

1. Open your phone's **Settings** app (the one with the gear/cog icon).

2. Tap on **Network & internet** (on some phones it's called **Connections**).

3. Tap **Data Saver** (it may be inside a section called "Data usage" on some phones).

4. You should see a switch that's currently on — **tap it to turn it OFF**. It should turn grey.

Once you've done that, come back to your home screen and check the top of your phone — the "Data Saver" message with the down arrow should be gone.

Could you give that a go and tell me what you see? Take your time with the Settings menus — if a heading looks slightly different to what I've described, just tell me what options you can see and I'll point you to the right one.

Once it's off, we'll do one final speed check to make sure your internet is running as it should be.
turns.execution_output: User: Alright, I'm going into the Settings... let me find that Data Saver switch and turn it off.

turns.thought:
Everything you've described tells me your connection is now set up correctly, John — you've done all the hard work!

Here's where things stand:

- ✅ **Airplane Mode** — off, and you have **Excellent** signal strength
- ✅ **5G** — connected to the fastest network available
- ✅ **Mobile Data** — enabled
- ✅ **Data Saver** — off, so nothing is restricting your speed
- ✅ **International roaming** — already active on your line for France
- ✅ **2 GB of extra data** — added for $4.00

I'm afraid I'm not able to run a speed test myself from my end — that has to happen on your device. But the simplest way for you to check is just to **open your web browser and try loading a page**, or open an app that needs the internet.

Could you try that and let me know how it goes? If pages load quickly, you're all set. If it still feels slow or doesn't load, tell me and we'll keep investigating.

One last tip for the road: **on 28 February your data allowance resets**, and that $4.00 refuel is a one-off for this month — it won't repeat next month. So you'll be back to your normal 15 GB with no extra charge.

Try the browser and let me know what happens!
turns.execution_output: User: Alright, let me try that speed check on my phone...

turns.thought:
You haven't done anything wrong at all, John — please don't worry. You've followed my instructions perfectly, and everything you've done is correct. There's just one more setting we need to look at, and it's the one that matters most while you're in France.

Here's the thing: when you're **abroad**, your phone connects to a French network instead of our own. Your phone has a separate switch for this, called **Data Roaming**. If that switch is off, you can have full signal and 5G showing — exactly as you do — but still have no internet, because your phone is refusing to use the foreign network. That fits your symptoms perfectly.

Let's check it:

1. Open **Settings** (the gear/cog icon).
2. Tap **Network & internet** (or **Connections**).
3. Tap **Mobile network** (sometimes called **SIMs** or **Mobile data**).
4. Look for **Roaming** or **Data roaming** and tap it.
5. Make sure **Data roaming** is switched **ON**.

Once that's on, go back to your home screen and try loading a web page again, or re-run the speed test.

Could you do that and tell me what happens? Take your time with it.

If the switch is already on, or if it still says no connection afterwards, don't worry — we'll move on to the next possibility. There are a couple more things we can try, and I'll stay with you until this is sorted.
turns.execution_output: User: Alright, let me go into the settings and find that roaming switch... I'm turning it on now.

turns.thought:
I've just double-checked your account, John, and I can confirm every point:

- ✅ **Your data is working** — 275 Mbps is excellent, and that's a genuinely fast connection.
- ✅ **Plan unchanged** — you're still on the **Premium Plan** (P1002) at **$65.00/month**. Your last plan change was back on 15 December 2024, so nothing has been changed today.
- ✅ **The $4.00 is one-time only** — it's a single charge on your current bill for this billing period. It will not repeat.
- ✅ **Your normal 15 GB returns on 28 February** — that's when your cycle resets, and you'll be back to your usual allowance with no extra charge.

**One small thing worth mentioning:** your refuelled 2 GB is additive to this month — but since you'd already used 15.1 GB of your 15 GB, you effectively have the 2 GB to carry you through to the 28th. So do try to keep usage modest over the next few days, or you might find it cuts out again before the reset.

**Also, since you're in France:** do keep **Data Roaming switched on** for the rest of your trip — that's the setting that got you connected. If you turn it off, you'll lose data again even though you'll still see 5G and full signal.

You've done really well today — you identified several settings yourself. Nothing you pressed could have harmed your photos; those are stored safely on your phone and aren't affected by any of the settings we changed.

Enjoy your time in France, and do get in touch if anything else comes up. Safe travels!
turns.execution_output:
User: Thank you so much — that's all very reassuring. I'll keep the roaming switched on and try not to use too much data before the 28th.

I really appreciate your patience with me. My internet is fast now and my plan is unchanged, so I'm happy. Have a lovely day!

###STOP###
